TODDLER ROOM LESSON · TODDLER ROOM · AGES 1–3 YEARS

Stroller — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches "stroller" as the family vehicle: the climb is the child’s job, the buckle’s click is the finisher, and teddy’s stroller rehearses the whole ride.

What is this?

The stroller is the blue pushchair by the door — the vehicle that carries little legs when little legs are done, and the routine word that makes leaving the park survivable.

What does it mean?

The stroller word lives where friction lives: getting in, getting out, leaving the fun. A named climb-in-click script turns the two worst moments of any outing into known steps.

What does the child need to know?

You need the stroller, the climb (child-powered with a hand nearby) and the click: the final buckle snap belongs to the child. Then the teddy stroller for rehearsal at home.

Why this matters

A child who climbs in themselves and clicks themselves is a passenger with ownership — and passengers with ownership disembark with dignity when the ride is over.

What it teaches

Climbing control, buckle manipulation (fine motor), leaving-the-fun transitions, and the pushing-the-teddy empathy loop.

Words to learn

strollerclimb inbuckleclickpushoff we go

Say this to your child

“"Stroller! Climb in — up you go! Buckle the straps… and CLICK! You did it. Off we go — wheels go round! And when the ride is done, click again — you hop out, big and safe."”

Step by step

  1. At the stroller: "stroller! Time to climb in."
  2. The child-powered climb — hand hovering, not hauling: "up you go!"
  3. Buckle together, child finishes: "click! Ready to roll."
  4. At home, the rehearsal: teddy rides the toy stroller — "push teddy… teddy is safe and cozy!" The driver learns what passengers feel.
  5. On outings, the same two words every time: "stroller — climb in!" and "stroller — click!" Sameness is the secret.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the word "stroller" sits under a blue pushchair — seat back, wheels ready, parked exactly where the outing begins.

Ask your child

"Where do you ride?" (the stroller) "Who clicks the buckle?" (me!) "Where does teddy sit?" (in HIS stroller)

What your child can say or do

Your child might say "stroller!" at the park gate, climb and click unprompted, or push teddy on serious rounds — the vehicle, fully staffed.

Out in the real world

Strollers park outside shops, fold into cars, queue at airports. Every sighting is a name-check: "stroller — like yours!" The word rides along.

Try it together

Teddy Bus Route: the toy stroller does the circuit — teddy on at the sofa stop, off at the kitchen stop, next passenger please. The toddler is driver, conductor and mechanic.

Understanding check

Ask: "What is this?" (stroller) "Who clicks the buckle?" "Show me climb in!" — climb, click, ride: the family vehicle is run by its passenger.

This lesson pairs with the Stroller flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Toddler Room.
